original_question: Does there exist, in ZFC, a set of reals with the Menger property U_fin(O, O) but without the Hurewicz property U_fin(O, Γ)?
target_in_paper: Section 5 ("Classification in ZFC"), Problem 2: "Does there exist (in ZFC) a set of reals X which has the Menger property Ufin(O, O) but not the Hurewicz property Ufin(O, Γ)?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact ambient setting (a set of reals), the exact logical form (existence in ZFC), and the exact pair of properties singled out in the paper: the Menger property Ufin(O,O) versus the Hurewicz property Ufin(O,Γ). It is essentially the paper's Problem 2 stated almost verbatim.
missing_details: The paper's standing scope is that, unless stated otherwise, spaces X are taken to be spaces homeomorphic to sets of reals.
In Section 2.1, Ufin(U,V) means: for every sequence (U_n) of members of U with no finite subcover, there are finite (possibly empty) F_n ⊆ U_n such that {⋃F_n : n ∈ N} belongs to V.
In Section 3, a 'cover' is explicitly required to be nontrivial: X = ⋃U and X is not itself a member of U.
O denotes the family of open covers of X.
Γ denotes the family of open γ-covers of X, i.e. infinite open covers in which each x ∈ X belongs to all but finitely many members.
For sets of reals, the paper notes that these covers may be assumed countable.
Section 4 records the equivalence Ufin(O,V) = Ufin(Γ,V) for every class V of covers, so the problem has an equivalent Γ-first-coordinate reformulation.
refined_question: In ZFC, does there exist a set of reals X such that X satisfies Ufin(O,O) but fails Ufin(O,Γ), where O is the family of nontrivial open covers of X, Γ is the family of open γ-covers of X, and Ufin(U,V) means that for every sequence (U_n) of members of U having no finite subcover, there exist finite sets F_n ⊆ U_n such that the family {⋃F_n : n ∈ N} belongs to V?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, by the paper's observation that Ufin(O,V) = Ufin(Γ,V) for every V, does there exist in ZFC a set of reals X with Ufin(Γ,O) but not Ufin(Γ,Γ)?
justification: The draft matches the paper's exact target: Section 5, Problem 2. To make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, the refinement only unpacks notation that is defined earlier in the paper: the selection principle Ufin(U,V) from Section 2.1, the standing restriction to spaces homeomorphic to sets of reals from Section 2.3, the meanings of cover, O, and Γ from Section 3, and the explicit equivalence Ufin(O,V)=Ufin(Γ,V) from Section 4. I therefore kept the question narrow and did not broaden it beyond the paper's original 'set of reals' formulation.
